recommendation_summary: The reply recommends wrapping the 03:00 cron entry with `|| mail ...` so that any nonzero exit or crash of `nightly-sync` sends a failure alert (or a push notification), with no Docker or Synology involved.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You (just now) need to know within hours, not days, when `nightly-sync` dies, without reading logs.
labels.Deleted: A Synology Docker log stack (Loki/Grafana/Dozzle-style central logging). You have one job on one machine; aggregating logs across services solves a problem you don't have, and a log store doesn't alert you on its own, so it wouldn't have caught last week's silence either.
labels.Bottleneck: The only alert path today is the email the script sends at the very end, so any crash before that point (like the expired token) is invisible. Fix needs to live outside the script, at the point it's invoked.
labels.Checked myself: Based only on what you told me, one cron job on edna, crash was pre-email, nothing else monitors it.

note: Single cron-level failure alert recommended now; the dead-man ping is conditionally deferred and the Synology/Docker log stack is explicitly rejected.
